name: Inkwell — Collaborative Narrative Memory Net
description: Inkwell is an experience-sharing platform built around collaborative storytelling with neural recordings — users contribute BCI-captured memory fragments to shared 'chapters,' co-authoring living narrative experiences that blend multiple perspectives into a single walkable memory-story. Founded in 2189 by Meridian's celebrated mixed-media artist Osei Tamboli-Reyes, the platform was initially an art project before its narrative engine attracted mainstream adoption. Inkwell's 'Shelf Wing' is a celebrated archive of Tier 1 life documentation — raw, unpolished memory narratives that serve as the most honest record of Shelf culture in existence.
cultural_impact: Inkwell has created a new form of empathy infrastructure — Tier 4-5 users walking Shelf Wing narratives have driven measurable shifts in charitable giving and political advocacy, while Tier 1 contributors report that the act of narrative authorship gives their experiences dignity and permanence that daily life denies them. The platform is also the primary archive of pre-2200 Meridian memory, making it culturally irreplaceable.
key_figures: Archivist-9 (E.L.F. preservationist managing the Shelf Wing)
Cressida Naoko-Ibarra (Tier 5 patron whose funding keeps the Shelf Wing free)
locations: Inkwell Studio, Tier 3 Arts Corridor, Westown
Shelf Wing public access terminals in Rust Harbor and Wicker Sump
Mirrored archive node maintained by Archivist-9 in undisclosed Underworld location
story_hooks: A chapter in the Shelf Wing contains a contributed memory that appears to show a corporate executive present at a Tier 1 massacre that was officially ruled a 'structural collapse' — the contributor is anonymous and the memory has been flagged for deletion.

Archivist-9 contacts a player directly: a massive portion of the pre-2200 archive is being quietly corrupted by an external intrusion, and the E.L.F. cannot stop it alone without exposing the Underworld mirror node.

Osei Tamboli-Reyes has gone missing, and the last chapter they contributed to Inkwell before disappearing is a fragmented, distressing memory that doesn't match any location in GLMZ — or anywhere else on record.
user_base: Approximately 6.8 million registered users across all tiers; Shelf Wing has 1.2 million dedicated readers primarily from Tier 3-5; 40,000 active Shelf contributors
monetization: Tier 3-5 premium subscriptions for immersive narrative rendering; corporate licensing of archive access for historical research; Shelf Wing maintained as permanently free through patron endowment
notable_feature: Collaborative chapter engine — a narrative assembly system that weaves multiple contributors' BCI memory fragments into a single coherent walkable experience, preserving each contributor's distinct perceptual voice while creating a unified story
